ruleName: Relief for Ball in Penalty Area
title: Lateral Relief from a Red Penalty Area
question: After your ball comes to rest in a red penalty area, how far from the point where the ball last crossed the edge of the penalty area may you drop under the lateral relief option?

choices.text: As far back as you wish.

explanation: When taking lateral relief from a red penalty area under Rule 17.1d(3), you must drop the ball within two club-lengths of the point where the ball last crossed the edge of the penalty area, not nearer the hole.

juniorVersion.title: Dropping Your Ball Next to a Red Penalty Area
juniorVersion.question: If your ball goes into a red penalty area, how far from where it went in can you drop your ball to play your next shot?

choices.text: As far back as you want.

juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball stops in a red penalty area, you can drop your ball within two club-lengths from where it went into the area, but not closer to the hole.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place on the golf course marked with red lines or stakes, like a pond or stream, where it’s hard to play your ball.
The length of your longest club, except the putter. You can use it to measure how far to drop your ball.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show the two club-length area with clubs on the ground and ask the child to walk where they can drop the ball. Let them help measure with a club.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they can drop the ball anywhere or as far as they want from the penalty area.
They might measure with a putter instead of their longest club (not the putter).
